title: Zero test on a nonzero register
statement: Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, with label $\ell$, register $r$, labels $\ell_0,\ell_1$, register assignment $\rho$, and input position $p$. Suppose the instruction at $\ell$ branches to $\ell_0$ when register $r$ is zero and to $\ell_1$ otherwise, and suppose $\rho(r)\ne 0$. Then for every output string $o$, within at most one step the program reaches $\ell_1$ with registers $\rho$, input position $p$, and output $o$.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction at $\ell$ is a zero test on register $r$ with destinations $\ell_0,\ell_1$
The claim holds for every initial output string $o$
replaced:
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, $r$ a register and $\ell$ a
label whose instruction is $\mathsf{jz}(r, \ell_0, \ell_1)$, ``go to $\ell_0$ if
register $r$ is zero, else to $\ell_1$''.  If the registers $\rho$ satisfy
$\rho(r) \ne 0$, then for every input position $p$, from label $\ell$ with
registers $\rho$ and $p$ symbols read the program reaches label $\ell_1$ with
registers $\rho$ and $p$ symbols read within one step, printing nothing.
